sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 (buzz-app) README
sources.locator: README.md: Get started; Preview limitations; Plugins
sources.finding: Buzz 1.0 is a desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) whose identity is a locally stored private key, with import from Buzz 0.X. Agents belong to a community; harnesses are Claude (Claude account, macOS/Linux), Codex (ChatGPT or OpenAI account, macOS/Linux), Goose (provider key) and Pi (API key, Node 22.19+). Local agents run while Buzz is open and work in ~/.buzz by default, able to run commands and edit files there. Talk via New chat with the default agent, a DM, or an @mention in a channel. The buzz CLI is bundled. Preview: builds come from main with no stable channel, plugin API is a preview that updates can break, agents from 0.X are imported with Import them now.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 (buzz-app) Agents reference
sources.locator: docs/agents.md: Creating and changing agents from a conversation; Turns a close or reload stopped; Saved Solo follow-ups; Sharing and exporting agents
sources.finding: agent_create and agent_update submit unsaved drafts the owner reviews and saves. Closing or reloading the app stops in-page Claude, Codex and goose turns; on next start Resume gives interrupted mentions back to the saved session (goose opens a new session) while queued mentions and watch turns are not kept. Saved Solo follow-ups survive restarts and use an outbox with receipts and per-row locks so another window cannot send twice. Share/export carries name, instructions, runtime, provider, model and picture, never workspace, keys, environment or memory.

sources.locator: docs/agents.md: External app authorization; Durable external approval
sources.finding: Local apps request agent MCP access via buzz://mcp-authorize; the owner chooses Authorize or Deny, version-2 approval lasts 30 days unless renewed by reconnect, and Settings > External apps offers Revoke access. Access is limited to community origins compiled in through BUZZ_EXTERNAL_MCP_COMMUNITIES.

sources.finding: BUZZ_EXTERNAL_MCP_COMMUNITIES defaults to empty, which disables external MCP access in all communities; "this repository's workflow sets none", so builds from this repository have no external app access unless a distributor compiles a list.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 (buzz-app) Usage
sources.locator: docs/agents.md: Usage
sources.finding: Usage, a default-off Settings destination under Plugins, shows the selected community's local agents' estimated cost vs the previous period, tokens (input, cache reads and writes), cache hit rate, daily cost by agent type and the costliest sessions, each opening its thread. Claude, Codex, Goose and Pi readers include subagent sessions; it reads 30 days once, then on Refresh or agent changes; costs come from the harness or published list prices and are marked a best-effort estimate, not a bill, which may differ from subscription or provider billing. Totals are per session, not per task.

sources.finding: Interests own event, timer and plugin-source subscriptions that wake agents; timers keep occurrence and expiry budgets; a completed source or spent timer is removed after its final queued turn succeeds; a failed source delivery keeps the subscription and output; failed event-watch reads retry after a backoff. The GitHub PR source needs a signed-in gh CLI.

sources.finding: Composer Model and effort apply per send. Work in a new worktree makes agents change a repository in a new worktree and branch. The live activity bubble opens an agent's activity and offers Stop (availability depends on agent type; for native Claude, Codex and Goose it also cancels pending plugin tool calls). Agent-to-agent dispatches, handoffs and results stay as collapsed history. A remote execution choice survives app restarts; if the target cannot be restored Buzz shows an error and needs a new session; remote Claude usage totals and transcripts are unavailable. The GitHub pull request panel shows Summary and Changes, holds unsent reviews in Submit review (Changes and Submit review need gh signed in) and offers Queue for merge, which queues the displayed commit while GitHub controls the merge.

sources.title: Buzz support: Choose and set up an agent
sources.locator: #agents
sources.finding: Harnesses include Claude, Codex, Goose, Pi and Builderlab (hosted), which runs on a cloud computer paid from workspace funds; local harnesses need the computer and provider sign-in. Paid remote agents and Builderlab inference are US-only. Memory: agents save facts in a Memory tab the owner can review and ask to correct or remove; core memory is supplied each turn; memories stay within their community. Attention Interests watch events or timers and can be paused; local agents need Buzz and the computer running. Each agent signs with its own key, tied to its owner by a signed ownership proof.

sources.title: Buzz support: Funds, usage, and billing
sources.locator: #funds
sources.finding: Paid services are for eligible residents of the 50 US states and DC; early-access or trial accounts may not show Add funds. Workspace prepaid funds pay data ($0.15 per GB-month or GB delivered after 100 GB included monthly per workspace), cloud compute ($0.65 per vCPU-hour while running, per second) and inference at Databricks list prices ($0.07 per DBU), deducted daily. A 4-vCPU hour costs $2.60. Workstations suspend after 5 idle minutes. One-time top-ups of $5-$1,000; no platform fee, recurring payment or monthly minimum. Communities must be allowed to use the balance. Purchased credits are generally non-refundable; promotional credits exist. Connected provider accounts bill separately.

sources.title: Buzz support: Manage remote agents
sources.locator: #remote-agents
sources.finding: Hosted agents are created in the desktop app with the Builderlab (hosted) harness; remote workstations offer 1-8 vCPU with 8 GiB per vCPU, suspend after 5 idle minutes, and can be shared by all agents (default) or separated per thread or per channel, which keeps working state apart. Shared remote instructions take up to 20,000 characters.

sources.title: Buzz support: Create a hosted community

sources.title: Buzz pricing (rendered from the site bundle)
sources.locator: plans; rates; Start free
sources.finding: Community: free self-hosted open-source Buzz. Pay as you go: no payment method to start, 100 GB shared data monthly and 10 static plus 10 dynamic apps, with remote agents, managed inference, pooled workspace billing and usage dashboard and spend controls. Enterprise: custom agreement via Contact sales with dedicated tenancy, SSO, custom SLA and "Negotiated rates and annual commitment". Rates: data $0.15, compute $0.65 per vCPU-hour, inference by model. "No monthly minimum." Paid remote agents and inference are US-only.

sources.title: Buzz Privacy Notice (rendered from the site bundle)
sources.locator: Analytics Technologies; Search and indexing; disclosures; retention; rights; international transfers
sources.finding: Consent is obtained for analytics and tracking where law requires. Search ML models are "designed to identify relevant results ... without learning, memorizing or reproducing" message content; no wider training statement is made. Disclosures go to vendor categories (cloud storage, analytics, generative AI, payments) and to AI model providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic for enabled agents; no named subprocessor list. User content is retained up to 365 days by default; rights requests (access, deletion, portability) go by email with verification. Transfers outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland rely on adequacy decisions or other mechanisms; no storage location is named.

sources.title: Buzz Terms of Service (rendered from the site bundle)
sources.locator: Free Services; Purchased Credits; metered usage
sources.finding: Free Services exist alongside Paid Services; Block-Provided Models are resold from providers including Databricks. Purchased Credits are non-transferable, non-refundable except as required or stated, and do not expire while the account is active; an insufficient balance can reject, pause, throttle or limit Paid Services.

sources.locator: cmd_create_issue, cmd_get_issue, cmd_list_issues, cmd_assign_issue, cmd_unassign_issue, cmd_issue_status and reduce_assignment_operations; command declarations under crates/buzz-cli/src; parse_status in commands/patches.rs

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 memory and context implementation
sources.locator: MemoryEntry and memoryListing; core-memory-cache.ts; docs/agent-memories.md Consumers/Budgets; src/buzz-mcp memory tools; bundled/codex/codex.sh
sources.finding: Agent memory entries have a slug, body, signed event ID and creation time. Core memory is cached per agent/community and refreshed after turns and reconnects; version checks protect edits, and non-core deletion uses tombstones. The pinned memory documentation says no plugin currently exposes a Memories UI, unlike the live support page that describes a Memory tab. Agent tools remain available. sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 repository and knowledge inspection
sources.locator: src/bundled/repos; src/buzz-mcp/tools.ts read/search and mem_get; src/features/search; src/bundled/github; searches for code search, symbol index, embedding, citation, conflict detection and specification enforcement
sources.finding: The app browses repository files, commits, issues and PRs, searches permitted relay conversations, and lets harness tools read working files. No product-owned semantic code/symbol index or architecture/specification conflict gate was found in these paths. Relay message search is not repository indexing. Retrieved messages and memory expose event identities, without a mandatory answer-citation policy.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 scheduling and recovery
sources.locator: QUEUE_LIMIT, INTEREST_LANES, INTEREST_LIMIT, TIMEOUT_LIMIT_MS, RATE_LIMIT; enqueue, next, drain, claim, start; interrupted.ts; searches for CPU, RAM, budget, retries, fairness and check deduplication
sources.finding: A runner has a FIFO mention lane plus up to eight concurrent Attention Interest lanes, each serial, with 32 queued jobs per mention/watch lane, eight queued jobs per Interest, 60 starts per minute per mention/watch rate lane and a 30-minute maximum requested deadline. Device custody prevents duplicate ownership across app copies on that machine; it is not a cross-host work lock. Queue overflow reports busy, and reconnect/catch-up retains bounded event checkpoints. No CPU/RAM-aware scheduler or shared verification deduplication was found.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 harness sessions and permissions
sources.locator: thread/start, thread/resume, sandbox danger-full-access, approvalPolicy never, mcp_servers; bundled/claude-code/claude.ts permission-mode bypassPermissions; bundled/goose and pi runtime registration; docs/agents.md local lifecycle
sources.finding: Buzz controls Codex through app-server sessions, Claude through its stream-json integration, Goose through ACP and Pi through its plugin host. Model/effort choices are supplied per turn. Ordinary Codex turns use danger-full-access with approvals never and Claude uses bypassPermissions. Extra MCP servers can come from harness configuration; this is separate from exposing Buzz tools to external apps.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 execution and workspace boundaries
sources.locator: docs/agents.md Plugin execution; src/bundled/{codex,claude-code}/execution.ts; src/bundled/builderlab/agents; searches for Kubernetes, container, VM, sandbox, port allocation, dependency cache and snapshot
sources.finding: Execution plugins can bind native harnesses to remote targets and retain a conversation execution key/workspace across restarts. The plugin owns target allocation, credentials, expiry and file policy; a missing target requires a new session. No bundled 0.X Kubernetes provider is registered in v1.0.6. Local agents share app-user OS authority, with optional branch/worktree file separation. Builderlab infrastructure isolation and host repair cannot be established from the client code.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 GitHub review and shipping actions
sources.locator: mutationOf and changePull lines 310-380; gh.ts gitHubDiff; SubmitReview.tsx; PullChecklist.tsx; watch.ts; index.tsx UI wiring
sources.finding: The GitHub panel submits COMMENT/APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES reviews for commitOID, reads a diff pinned to the displayed head, merges/enqueues/enables auto-merge or updates a branch using expectedHeadOid, and displays repository checks/reviews/conflicts. A signed-in gh process supplies GitHub authority. GitHub owns branch rules and the merge queue. No product-owned cross-task delivery gate, release workflow, rollback or batch risk/size queue was found in the panel and agent tools.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 per-turn code change cards
sources.locator: bundled/changesets README and plugin hooks; src/bundled/index.ts enablement; searches for gallery, review evidence, task/revision link and retained changes
sources.finding: The opt-in Changesets plugin snapshots local Git project folders before/after an agent turn and displays file diffs under its last message. It keeps 300 turns in device local storage, excludes files over 5 MB and caps at 1,000 changed files. Concurrent writers can contaminate attribution, and remote agents are not tracked. General attachments, canvases and PR panels are separate from a cross-task artifact gallery.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 verification guidance and enforcement inspection
sources.locator: engineering.md; src/bundled/github/{PullChecklist,pull,watch}; src/bundled/builderlab/apps; src/buzz-mcp/session-tools.ts; searches for required tests, spec gate, independent review, delivery status, stale approval and rollback
sources.finding: The shipped prompt tells agents to verify relevant work and seek a second opinion on risky changes. This is guidance, not an enforced test/lint/types/specification gate. GitHub checks and head-bound actions can enforce repository policy through GitHub. Builderlab deploy APIs retain version/deployment IDs but are not a required test/review approval gate. No product-owned task delivery or stale task-approval invalidation model was found.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 human input and ownership inspection
sources.locator: mention routing, owner/agent authorization and ordered queues; docs/solo/sharing.md; src/bundled/channels; src/features/agent-harness/sections/{trust,routing,callbacks}.md; searches for ownership transfer and co-prompting
sources.finding: Shared channels have signed attributed messages and membership/role access, but ordinary local agent invocation is restricted to its owner, verified agent-origin delegation and its own watches. Sharing a channel does not by itself authorize every colleague to command an owner-controlled coding agent. The mention queue orders accepted input; no general cross-user conflict resolver or owner-transfer operation was found.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 supplied delegation instructions and tools
sources.locator: routing.md, callbacks.md, tools.md, autonomy.md, sections/compose.ts and src/buzz-mcp/tools.ts send/read/agent tools; runner delegated message admission
sources.finding: Buzz ships instructions to assign work to other agents in the originating channel and return completed results or blockers by mentioning the delegator. Its messaging tools send and inspect that channel, and the runner admits authorized agent-origin delegation. Creating/changing agents or teams submits an owner-reviewed draft rather than silently starting arbitrary children. Retained channel messages show exchanges; a separate parent/child orchestration tree is not supplied. Delegated invocation is limited to verified common-owner sibling identities; unrelated human or agent messages do not acquire authority from channel membership.

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 local diagnostics controls
sources.locator: performanceDiagnostics enabledByDefault false; src/bundled/performance-diagnostics; docs/client-metrics.md; src/features/developer/client-metrics.ts; searches for analytics, Sentry and telemetry in src/app, src/shared and src-tauri/src

sources.title: Buzz 1.0.6 owner and sibling invocation authority
sources.locator: mentionAuthority, fromOwner, attestedOwner and ownedCreator; runtime/runner call sites; src/features/agent-harness/sections/trust.md
